situation:
You are the Director of Client Marketing and the Placement Operations Manager at TIDEMARK STAFFING GROUP, a regional staffing agency that recruits and places hourly workers with employers across the coast. The founder (judge) has asked the two of you to meet about a contract offer that has to be answered this week, and to bring a recommendation rather than a summary.

Tidemark opened two years ago on a single promise its marketing has repeated ever since: the agency walks and clears every site before it places anyone there. That promise is what wins work against larger agencies competing on price, and it is why lodging clients keep calling. The first round of funding that built the recruiting team has about five months of payroll left.

HARBORLIGHT INNS, Tidemark's largest lodging client, has offered a three-year contract as one package. Half of it staffs the reservations office where guests book rooms directly by phone, through the chain's own website, and at the front desk. The other half staffs CEDARFLOW LINEN WORKS, the laundry facility Harborlight owns, which is nine months into a state compliance schedule for wastewater discharge from its bleaching line. Harborlight will not split the two.

Tidemark has placed a small crew at Cedarflow for fourteen months. Its placement data is unusually good: retention above the agency average, no filed safety complaints, and satisfaction scores that beat every warehouse account on the books. The senior placement coordinator who has walked that floor reads it differently, reporting that workers describe stinging eyes near the discharge line and ask quietly to be moved, and that no one raises such a thing on a survey while hours are at stake.

Signing the package covers payroll past the compliance schedule and secures the reservations work Tidemark has wanted for a year, but it commits crews to a floor the agency's own coordinator will not vouch for and rests the vetting promise on numbers that coordinator distrusts. Declining the facility means declining the whole contract, which leaves Tidemark raising money on short notice or cutting the recruiters who make the promise true.

The founder (judge) wants your recommendation on whether Tidemark should sign the Harborlight package as offered, and on how the agency should weigh its own placement data against what its most experienced coordinator reports from the floor. The founder (judge) will greet you both and ask to hear your ideas. After your presentation and any questions, the founder (judge) will thank you both and close the meeting.
